title: Imaging Denatured Collagen Strands In vivo and Ex vivo via Photo-triggered Hybridization of Caged Collagen Mimetic Peptides
protocol: Prepare 110 µl of caged CMP solution for each mouse.
Mix 11 µl of IR680-Ahx-NB(GPO)9 stock solution (400 µM) with 11 µl of 100 µM cysteine in sterile PBS solution.
Bring the total volume to 110 µl with 1x PBS buffer.
Slowly withdraw the peptide solution into a 0.5 ml insulin syringe with a transparent barrel and a small gauge (28-30 G) needle.
Carefully remove air bubbles from the syringe.
Turn on the UV lamp for 2-5 min to warm up.
Place the peptide-containing syringe directly under the UV lamp (365 nm, >25 mW/cm²) for 5 min.
Position the mouse in a restrainer under a heated lamp.
Label the mouse with a permanent marker on the tail or use other identification methods such as ear tag or toe tattoo.
Disinfect the tail of the mouse with 70% alcohol.
Inject 100 µl of UV-activated IR680-Ahx-NB(GPO)9 solution into the tail vein of the mouse.
Place the mouse back in its cage after injection.
Set the heater plate of the imaging bed to 37 °C using Pearl Impulse 2.0 software.
Put the nude or shaved mouse into the anesthesia induction chamber containing 2% isoflurane in oxygen.
Verify depth of anesthesia by checking for lack of movement during handling and monitoring respirations (~1/sec).
Open the Pearl imager drawer and place the anesthetized animal on the imaging bed.
Remove the nose cone plug and slide the mouse's muzzle inside the nose cone to maintain anesthesia.
Close the drawer containing the mouse.
Click the "700 channel," "white light" and "85 micron" boxes in Image software when the instrument indicates "ready."
Acquire NIR (excitation 685 nm, emission 720 nm) and white light photographs using automatic focus and exposure.
Prepare 1 ml of 10% (w/v) BSA solution in deionized water.
Thaw 1 ml of goat serum in a water bath at room temperature.
Cut pieces of Parafilm in the size of approximately 2 cm x 5 cm.
Prepare 10 ml of blocking buffer by mixing 500 µl of goat serum, 1 ml of 10x PBS and 8.5 ml of deionized water.
Prepare 5 ml of CMP dilution buffer by diluting 50 µl of 10% (w/v) BSA with 4.45 ml of deionized water and 500 µl 10x PBS.
Dilute stock solutions of carboxyfluorescein-labeled caged CMP, CFNB(GPO)9, from 480 µM to 5 µM using the CMP dilution buffer.
Store the formulated CMP solutions in darkness.
Let mouse cornea tissue slides equilibrate to room temperature.
Incubate the slides in 1x PBS buffer for 5 minutes.
Place the slides in a humidified chamber.
Apply 0.5 ml of blocking solution to each slide and incubate at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Remove the blocking solution by blotting the slides on paper towels.
Apply approximately 100 µl of CFNB(GPO)9 solutions to cover the tissue sections of each slide.
Incubate the slides for 2 minutes to allow the CMP solution to permeate the tissues.
Turn on the UV lamp and expose the CMP-covered tissue sections to UV light at 365 nm (~8 mW/cm²) for 6 minutes after the lamp is warmed up.
Cover the tissue sections of each slide with a piece of Parafilm to prevent drying.
Place the slides in the humidified chamber and incubate them at 4 °C for 2 hours.
Prepare a 1:3,000 dilution of DAPI solution in 1x PBS.
Gently remove the Parafilm with forceps after CMP staining.
Blot the slides on a paper towel to remove excess CMP solution.
Apply approximately 100 µl of diluted DAPI solution to each tissue slide.
Incubate for 1 min at room temperature.
Immerse the slides in 1x PBS buffer in a staining jar for 5 min.
Repeat this procedure 3 times in fresh 1x PBS to wash off unbound staining agents.
Add a drop of mounting medium on the tissue section.
Cover the tissue with a glass cover slip while avoiding trapping air bubbles.
Put the slides in a cardboard slide tray to protect them from light.
Image the collagen strands (FITC channel) and cell nuclei (DAPI channel) using a fluorescence microscope.
